title: 1978 AHSME Problem 26
statement: In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB=10,\) \(AC=8,\) and \(BC=6.\) Circle \(P\) is the circle with smallest radius which passes through \(C\) and is tangent to \(AB.\) Let \(Q\) and \(R\) be the points of intersection, distinct from \(C,\) of circle \(P\) with sides \(AC\) and \(BC,\) respectively. The length of segment \(QR\) is

solutions.text:
Let \(H\) be the foot of the altitude from \(C\) to \(AB.\) Among circles through \(C\) tangent to \(AB,\) the least radius occurs when the tangency point is \(H,\) so \(CH\) is a diameter. The area of the right triangle gives \[ CH=\frac{AC\cdot BC}{AB}=\frac{8\cdot6}{10}=4.8. \] Also \(\angle QCR=90^\circ,\) so \(QR\) is a diameter of circle \(P.\) Therefore \(QR=CH=4.8.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: The \(6\)-\(8\)-\(10\) triangle is right at \(C\); let \(H\) be the foot from \(C\) to \(AB\)
The smallest circle has \(CH\) as a diameter, and \(\angle QCR=90^\circ\)
